the immunization with a recombinant protein containing a tandem repeat peptide from the immunogenic dominant epitopes of foot-and-mouth-disease virus VP1 protein and beta-galacto-sidase induced a neutralizing antibody and a T-cell response in guinea pigs and in swine.
the recombinant fusion proteins containing beta-gal and a tandem repeat epitope elicit high levels of neutralization antibody and protect both guinea pigs against FMDV infection.

the construction of a recombinant protein and DNA vaccine against FMDV infection in guinea pigs and pigs.
the development of new vaccines against FMD.
the production of a novel recombinant protein and two DNA plasmids that elicit a high neutralizing antibody response in guinea pigs and a protective immune response in swine.

the recombinant fusion proteins and DNA vaccines are promising candidates for the control of foot-and-mouth diseases.

a recombinantly expressed fusion protein is a potent immunogen that induces a strong humoral and cellular immune response in guinea pigs and pigs and protects animals against challenge with FMDV.

the recombinant fusion proteins are effective vaccines for both swine and guinea pigs against foot-and-mouth disease, and DNA vaccines may be a good choice to protect guinea pigs from foot-and-mouth disease infection, but they are not effective for swine.

the recombinant fusion proteins and DNA plasmids can elicit a strong immune response and protect animals against foot-and-mouth disease infection, and these recombinant proteins and plasmids could be used as vaccines against foot-and-mouth virus infection.
